Subject: Re: DPA redlines — backup residency & deletion evidence request

Priya — thanks for the clear summary. We heard you and discussed internally with Legal + Ops. High-level proposal below; attaching a marked-up DPA and our backup-retention matrix for detail.

Proposal highlights (operational + legal):
- Primary production data: resident in EU region; customer may request single-region pinning per account.
- Backups/snapshots: geo-redundant by default (EU primary + EU secondary) — if cross-border replication is required for DR we will add an explicit access justification/approval workflow and log it.
- Retention windows: production TTL governed by contracted retention. Backups retained for a maximum of 90 days post-creation (snapshots included).
- Deletion evidence: for deletion requests we will provide a deletion manifest within 45 days for primary data and certification for backup purges within 90 days (manifest + audit log extract).
- Legal hold & incident holds: hold requests will freeze purge workflows; we propose a carveout that triggers a notification and preserves materials until lawful hold is lifted.

Operational cutover approach
- For accounts that require immediate EU-only residency for both primary and backups, we can perform a staged cutover: (1) snapshot existing data to EU-only storage, (2) validate manifests, (3) retire cross-border copies. Target timeline ~30–60 days depending on dataset size.

Attachments:
- Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf (redline with suggested text)
- backup-retention-matrix.xlsx (detailed schedule and operational notes)

If that aligns with Aurum’s tolerance, Laura can provide precise legal language for the DPA. Operationally Jordan will own the cutover runbook.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: DPA redlines — draft language for backup and deletion clauses

Hi Priya / Elaine —

Following Rishi’s proposal, suggested redline snippets for the DPA: replace Section 4.2 (Backups) with the following language: 

"Supplier shall ensure that Customer Data designated as EU-resident is stored in EU data centers for primary storage. Backups containing EU-resident Customer Data shall be maintained in EU-located storage unless cross-border replication is explicitly requested and approved in writing by Customer. Backups and snapshots shall be retained for no longer than ninety (90) days from the snapshot creation date. Supplier shall provide a deletion manifest and supporting audit log extracts within ninety (90) days following a Customer-initiated deletion request, and shall provide a manifest for primary data deletion within forty-five (45) days."

We will accept a 45/90 evidence timeline as a compromise, provided Redwood includes:
- A sample deletion manifest template (see attachments)
- A one-page attestation that an authorized operator performed the purge
- A process for validated secure deletion of on-disk copies and snapshots

Also requesting DocuSign-friendly wording for the hold carveout and an SLA for turnaround times on deletion evidence requests (we propose: initial acknowledgment within 5 business days; manifest within the 45/90 window).

Attached: legal-redlines-dpa.docx (tracked changes).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: legal-redlines-dpa.docx (docx)
